root_cause.text: `f_mass_storage`’s `check_command_size_in_blocks()` converted SCSI block counts to bytes by left-shifting `common->data_size_from_cmnd` by `common->curlun->blkbits` without any overflow check, so a large host-supplied READ/WRITE transfer size could wrap the value and defeat later bounds checks.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `common->data_size_from_cmnd <<= common->curlun->blkbits;` to `check_shl_overflow(common->data_size_from_cmnd, common->curlun->blkbits, &common->data_size_from_cmnd)` and returns `-EINVAL`/sets `phase_error` on overflow; the commit message explicitly says the old shift “does not validate whether this shift operation will cause an integer overflow” and can “wrap around” to a truncated size.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the overflow helper header so the file can use kernel overflow-checking utilities.
intent_record.what: A new include directive, `#include <linux/overflow.h>`, was added to the header list near the top of the file.
intent_record.how: This makes the overflow-checking helpers and related definitions from `linux/overflow.h` available to the translation unit, allowing code in this file to use kernel overflow validation macros or functions at compile time.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add overflow-safe command size scaling and fail the request on shift overflow.
intent_record.what: The code changed the block-size adjustment in check_command_size_in_blocks() from a direct left shift of common->data_size_from_cmnd by common->curlun->blkbits to a checked shift using check_shl_overflow(). If overflow is detected, it now sets common->phase_error to 1 and returns -EINVAL before calling check_command().
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now prevents undefined or wrapped results when converting a command size into blocks. If the shift would overflow, the request is rejected early with an error and the device enters a phase error state instead of continuing with a corrupted size value.
